costNote: Fuel and operating costs of the power plants and utilities — $2,890M. AES calls what remains 'operating margin' (25.4% of revenue, up from 21.9% a year ago).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Corporate overhead only. AES books its interest bill below this line (it appears in other expense here); plant-level running costs sit in cost of sales.

otherDetail.label: Interest expense
otherDetail.note: AES carries heavy project debt across its global fleet — the single biggest below-the-line cost.

otherDetail.label: Asset impairments
otherDetail.note: Write-downs of asset values in the quarter.

otherDetail.label: Extinguishment, FX & other, net
otherDetail.note: A $13M loss on early debt repayment, $14M of currency losses and $25M of other expense, partly offset by $21M of other income and a $3M disposal gain.

otherDetail.label: Equity earnings of affiliates
otherDetail.note: AES's share of joint-venture profits, reported after tax in its statement.

footerNote: AES did not furnish an earnings release this quarter; figures are from its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q (filed Nov 3, 2026). Net income is the consolidated $527M; $553M was attributable to AES because noncontrolling interests absorbed a $26M loss. AES presents interest expense inside its operating section; it is shown below the operating line here, as most companies present it.

segments.name: Non-regulated
segments.note: Contracted and merchant power: the Renewables unit ($1,104M of revenue) and Energy Infrastructure ($1,536M) — generation sold under long-term contracts and into markets.

segments.name: Regulated
segments.note: The Utilities unit ($1,256M before corporate/eliminations) — AES Ohio and AES Indiana earn regulated returns.

sources.label: AES Form 10-Q for Q3 2026 — SEC EDGAR (filed Nov 3, 2026)

takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $3.87B and operating margin widened from 21.9% to 25.4% — renewables growth plus stronger regulated and contracted generation.
takeaways.title: Top line and margin both up

takeaways.text: Asset impairments of $91M and a $361M interest bill are the drag: of $982M of operating margin, interest alone consumed more than a third.
takeaways.title: Impairments and interest bite

takeaways.text: Net income attributable to AES ($553M) is higher than the consolidated $527M because outside partners in AES subsidiaries absorbed a $26M loss — an unusual sign convention, disclosed in the footer.
takeaways.title: Attributable beats consolidated

verdict: Growth with leverage: revenue up 15.5% and margins wider, but a $361M quarterly interest bill and $91M of impairments take their cut.
